title: Purity for regular closed immersions
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion of pure codimension
$c$, with $X$ smooth over the perfect field $k$ and $Z$ regular.

*The fundamental class.* A *frame* of $Z$ is an étale
$U\to X$ together with $f_1,\dots,f_c\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ generating
the ideal of $Z_U=Z\times_XU$. Each $f_j$ is a unit on $U\setminus V(f_j)$,
so it has a Kummer class $\kappa(f_j)\in H^1(U\setminus V(f_j),\Lambda(1))$
as in [sk-def-purity-conv], and the boundary of the localization sequence
of $V(f_j)\subset U$ gives
$\partial\kappa(f_j)\in H^2_{V(f_j)}(U,\Lambda(1))$. The *class of
the frame* is the cup product with supports

$$
\operatorname{cl}(f)=\partial\kappa(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(f_c)
\ \in\ H^{2c}_{Z_U}\bigl(U,\Lambda(c)\bigr).
$$

Then:
- **(a)** $Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ with
$\mathcal H^0$ free of rank one; hence
$H^0(Z,Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c])=H^{2c}_Z(X,\Lambda(c))=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal H^0)$,
and likewise after any étale $U\to X$.
- **(b)** $\operatorname{cl}(f)$ depends only on $Z_U\subset U$, not on
the frame, and the frame classes glue to a unique global class, the
*fundamental class*

$$
[Z\subset X]=\operatorname{cl}_{Z/X}\ \in\ H^{2c}_Z\bigl(X,\Lambda(c)\bigr)
=H^0\bigl(Z,Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c]\bigr),
$$

which generates $\mathcal H^0$ at every geometric point. (The frame
classes and their gluing make sense for every regular closed immersion;
for the zero section of $\Aaf^1_Y$ the class so defined is
$\mathrm{pur}_s$ of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] with $c=1$, and for the zero section of $\Aaf^c_B$
it is the generator $\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$
of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity], by the definition of those classes; these pairs are
in the situation of the theorem when $Y$, resp. $B$, is smooth over $k$.)
- **(c)** The morphism

$$
\operatorname{cl}_i:\ \Lambda_Z\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ Ri^{!}\Lambda_X(c)[2c],
\qquad 1\longmapsto[Z\subset X],
$$

is an isomorphism, and it equals the isomorphism assembled from smooth
purity of $a_X$ and $a_Z$ in Steps 1–2 below. Since twists pass through
$Ri^{!}$ ([sk-lem-coprojection]), equivalently the inverse of
$\operatorname{cl}_i(-c)[-2c]$ is a canonical isomorphism

$$
Ri^{!}\Lambda_X\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c].
$$

- **(d)** It is compatible with étale base change,
$[Z_U\subset U]=[Z\subset X]|_U$, and with exterior products: for two such
pairs $(X_1,Z_1)$, $(X_2,Z_2)$ over $k$, the product
$(X_1\times_kX_2,Z_1\times_kZ_2)$ is again such a pair, of codimension
$c_1+c_2$, and
$[Z_1\times Z_2\subset X_1\times X_2]=[Z_1\subset X_1]\boxtimes[Z_2\subset X_2]$
under the exterior product of classes with supports.

proof.text:
*Step 1: the dualizing-object identification.* Work in the finite-coefficient, separated finite-type setting of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Components of $X$ disjoint from $Z$ contribute the zero category and need no dimension subtraction. On every other connected component, [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure] gives smooth $a_X$ and $a_Z=a_Xi$ of pure dimensions $n$ and $m=n-c$. The exceptional composition comparison for $i$, which need not be smooth, is obtained formally from [thm-sf-comp-composition] and the adjunctions of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: for every bounded constructible $M$ and $L$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,R(a_Xi)^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R(a_Xi)_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{X!}Ri_!M,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Ri^!Ra_X^!L).$$
Yoneda gives $c_{a_X,i}:Ra_Z^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!Ra_X^!$; the identity and associativity clauses of the compact-support theorem give those of this comparison. Write $\Pi_f:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(d)[2d]$ for the specified diagonal orientation of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]. In the notation of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], $\Pi_f^{-1}=\gamma_{f,\Lambda}$ after the unit identifications. Thus $\omega_Z\cong Ri^!\omega_X$, $\omega_X\cong\Lambda_X(n)[2n]$ and $\omega_Z\cong\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]$. The identifications assemble over the disjoint components.

proof.text:
*Step 2: cancel the twist and identify supported cohomology.* Use the pro-etale co-projection [lem-pur-coprojection] with $K=\Lambda_X$ and $L=\Lambda_X(n)[2n]$. The constant coefficient sheaf $K$ is bounded constructible, and $L$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude with tensor inverse $\Lambda_X(-n)[-2n]$; thus the finite-coefficient hypotheses of the current co-projection statement hold. For the last arrow below the same check uses the invertible factor $\Lambda_X(-m)[-2m]$. Step 1 then gives $Ri^!\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]$. Fix the direction of the resulting isomorphism $\Phi_i$ by the composite
$$\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\Pi_{a_Z}^{-1}(-m)[-2m]}\omega_Z(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{c_{a_X,i}}(Ri^!\omega_X)(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{Ri^!\Pi_{a_X}}(Ri^!\Lambda_X(n)[2n])(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!(\Lambda_X(c)[2c]),$$
where the last arrow uses co-projection and $n-m=c$. Consequently the target is a degree-zero sheaf isomorphic to $\Lambda_Z$. For $F=\Lambda_X(c)$, [lem-pur-supported-hom] identifies $H_Z^{2c}(X,F)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*\Lambda_Z,F[2c])$. For the closed immersion, [prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit] states $i_*=Ri_*=Ri_!$ with the compactification $(\operatorname{id}_Z,i)$. Apply the constructible adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] directly to $\Lambda_Z$ and $F[2c]$, both bounded constructible (indeed finite-Tor); it identifies this Hom group with $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_Z,Ri^!(F[2c]))=H^0(Z,Ri^!(F[2c]))$. For a degree-zero sheaf this is its group of sections. For an etale neighbourhood $u:U\to X$, the pullback $v:Z\times_XU\to Z$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], applied to the jointly surjective family $(u,\operatorname{id}_X)$ and base change by $i$. Thus the same argument applies on every such neighbourhood: smoothness and the relative dimensions persist by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and pulling a regular sequence through the flat etale local ring map preserves its successive injective multiplication maps [def-weil-etale-morphism, sk-def-purity-conv].

source.place: Step 2; expanded using the cited current DAG statements

proof.text: *Step 3: define the fundamental class.* For every frame, [def-pur-frame-class] defines the supported Kummer-boundary cup product, with the empty-frame unit when $c=0$. By [lem-pur-frame-independence] two frames of the same closed pair give the same class. Its hypotheses hold for every frame $u:U\to X$: $X$ and $Z$ are smooth over $k$ by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure], so $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Z_U\to Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] (the etale maps having relative dimension $0$); the relative dimension of $U$ over $k$ is locally constant, so one applies the definition and the lemma on each of the finitely many open and closed pieces of $U$ of constant relative dimension, the class on $U$ being the family of these classes; and $Z_U$ has pure codimension $c$ in $U$, since by Step 2 its ideal is generated near each point by a regular sequence of length $c$, and dividing a Noetherian local ring by a regular sequence lowers its dimension by the length of the sequence. Under Step 2 these are sections of the degree-zero sheaf on $Z$. Here restriction is the restriction of supported classes: the localization boundaries are functorial by [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and the supported-Hom construction in [lem-pur-supported-hom] commutes with restricting the closed-open pair. Frames exist Zariski-locally by the definition of regular immersion in [sk-def-purity-conv]. Pulling the frames to an overlap gives frames of the same pair, whose classes agree by frame independence; the sheaf axiom therefore glues them to a unique global section $[Z\subset X]$.

proof.text:
*Step 4: compare $\Phi_i(1)$ with the frame class.* For an etale map $u:U\to X$ put $V=Z\times_XU$ and write $v:V\to Z$, $i_U:V\hookrightarrow U$. Apply the canonical ordinary etale adjoint-locality comparison [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] to $f=\operatorname{id}_X$ and $u$, and to $f=\operatorname{id}_Z$ and $v$. Since the identity compact-support functor and its right adjoint are identities, it gives $u^{\times}\cong u^*$ and $v^{\times}\cong v^*$. Transport these comparisons on etale-origin bounded constructible inputs through the defining formula of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], obtaining $Ru^!\cong Lu^*$ and $Rv^!\cong Lv^*$. These etale maps are taken between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, hence satisfy the separatedness, finite-type and Noetherian hypotheses of the locality lemma; all maps admit the compactifications required there, as in the exceptional-functor definition. The smooth orientation agrees with this exact etale identification: the etale diagonal is open by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and closed by separatedness, and the projection restricted to that diagonal is the identity. The section invariant in [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] is therefore in the rank-zero coordinate model; [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] is the identity on that model, and [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] at $d=0$ fixes its affine comparison to be the identity. General exceptional composition from Step 1 gives the typed restriction identification
$$Ri_U^!Lu^*\cong Ri_U^!Ru^!\cong R(ui_U)^!=R(iv)^!\cong Rv^!Ri^!\cong Lv^*Ri^!.$$
The composition compatibility of the smooth orientations [thm-pur-composition-coherence], applied to the smooth pairs $(u,a_X)$ and $(v,a_Z)$, identifies the composite defining $\Phi_{i_U}$ with $Lv^*\Phi_i$ under this identification; twists move by [lem-pur-coprojection]. For $c\geq1$, [lem-pur-regular-immersion-linearization] supplies such a neighbourhood with an etale map $w:U\to\mathbf A^{c+m}_k$ and $V=w^{-1}(\mathbf A^m_k)$ scheme-theoretically; this is a pullback of the coordinate pair, not an isomorphism of $U$ with affine space. Put $f_j=w^*t_j$; these form a frame, which is enough by Step 3.
On the model let $p:\mathbf A^c_{\mathbf A^m}\to\mathbf A^m$ and $i_0$ be its zero section. Since $a_{\mathbf A^{c+m}}=a_{\mathbf A^m}p$ and $pi_0=\mathrm{id}$, smooth composition compatibility and Step 1 rewrite $\Phi_{i_0}$ as the inverse of
$$T:Ri_0^!\Lambda(c)[2c]\xrightarrow{Ri_0^!\gamma_{p,\Lambda}}Ri_0^!Rp^!\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda.$$
The smooth map is invertible by [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity], and [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement] identifies it with the ordered affine comparison. Precisely the last normalization clause of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] says $T^{-1}=\mathrm{th}_c$ and $\mathrm{th}_c(1)=\partial\kappa(t_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(t_c)$. Pullback of the Kummer class is natural by [sk-def-purity-conv]; boundaries are natural by [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. The cup product [def-pur-supported-cup] is formed by tensoring the supported-Hom morphisms, so restricting this composite tensors the restricted morphisms. Hence the restricted coordinate class is $\operatorname{cl}(w^*t_1,\ldots,w^*t_c)$, the frame class of [def-pur-frame-class]. For $c=0$, near any point of $Z$ the empty sequence generates the zero ideal, so $i$ is the identity pair there; the defining composite for $\Phi_{\mathrm{id}}$ cancels $\Pi_a^{-1}$ with $\Pi_a$, leaving the identity. Its class is the empty-frame unit, also the $c=0$ normalization in the cited affine-space corollary. These neighbourhoods cover $Z$, so $\Phi_i(1)=[Z\subset X]$. A morphism from $\Lambda_Z$ to a degree-zero sheaf is determined by the image of $1$; thus $\operatorname{cl}_i=\Phi_i$, proving (b),(c), including stalkwise generation.

proof.text:
*Step 5: compatibilities.* An etale base change pulls a frame back to a frame. The Kummer pullback of [sk-def-purity-conv], functorial localization boundary of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and tensor composite defining [def-pur-supported-cup] carry its class to the class of the pulled-back frame. Step 3 and uniqueness of gluing therefore give the asserted base-change identity; by Step 4 it is also the identity for the purity maps.
For products first verify the hypotheses. The schemes $X_j$ and $Z_j$ are smooth over $k$ by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure]. Base change and composition [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] show their products are smooth; regularity of the product of the $Z_j$ follows on affine smooth $k$-algebras from [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. For regularity of the immersion use affine regular frames $f$ in a $k$-algebra $R$ and $g$ in a $k$-algebra $S$, whose existence is part of [sk-def-purity-conv]. Tensoring the successive injective multiplication maps for $f$ with the $k$-vector space $S$ preserves injectivity. After quotienting by $f$, tensoring the successive multiplication maps for $g$ with the $k$-vector space $R/(f)$ also preserves injectivity. Thus $(f\otimes1,1\otimes g)$ is a regular sequence of length $c_1+c_2$ locally at every point of $Z_1\times Z_2$, where its final quotient is nonzero; its ideal is the kernel of $R\otimes_kS\to R/(f)\otimes_kS/(g)$. This proves the required pure codimension in the regular-sequence convention of [sk-def-purity-conv], including empty sequences.
On the resulting product frames the left-associated cup product for the concatenated tuple is
$\operatorname{pr}_1^*\operatorname{cl}(f)\cup\operatorname{pr}_2^*\operatorname{cl}(g)$: tensor associativity rebrackets the same ordered factors, with no permutation or sign. This is the supported exterior product of the two classes: the definition [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] tensors the pulled-back evaluation morphisms, and its coefficient comparison and the coefficient comparison in [def-pur-supported-cup] both restrict constants to the intersection and multiply them. Their composites agree on local tensor generators, hence agree as sheaf morphisms and on K-flat representatives. Consequently the two supported classes agree on these frames. Frame independence [lem-pur-frame-independence] and uniqueness of gluing give the required global exterior-product identity.
